title: How Does a Message Travel Across the Internet?
paragraphs: You send a message to a friend. It arrives in one second. How does it travel?
The computer cuts the message into small pieces. Each piece has an address. The address says where the piece must go.
Many machines help the pieces. These machines are called routers. They send each piece to the next machine, again and again.
At the end, your friend's phone gets all the pieces. It puts them together. Now your friend can read the message.
